pipeline.title: Reproduce: build a scenario tree with a normal file and a nested subdir matched by an ignore-paths regex, run PyLinter._discover_files + expand_modules on it with various invocation forms (bare relative dir, '.', trailing slash) to confirm which forms bypass the filter

Locate every place a discovered/candidate path is compared against ignore_list_paths_re: pylint/lint/pylinter.py _discover_files (root check) and pylint/lint/expand_modules.py _is_ignored_file/_is_in_ignore_list_re (top-level arg check and subfilepath check)

Determine why the regex fails to match: the string being tested still carries filesystem artifacts (leading './', OS-specific separators) that the anchored user-supplied pattern does not expect, because normalization (os.path.normpath) happens only after the ignore check, or not at all on some code paths

Fix by normalizing the path (os.path.normpath, and converting to a consistent separator via the existing regexp_paths_csv dual-pattern compile) before every ignore_list_paths_re comparison, in both _discover_files and expand_modules, so the same file is judged the same way regardless of how it was reached (top-level arg, os.walk root, or package sub-walk)

Verify: re-run the reproduction scenarios (bare dir, '.', trailing slash, package-with-__init__ case) and confirm the ignored subdir's files are absent from expand_modules' result in all of them; also run pylint's existing ignore-paths/recursive test suite

approaches.source: issue.md (bug report) + direct reproduction via pylint.lint.pylinter.PyLinter._discover_files and pylint.lint.expand_modules.expand_modules called on a scenario tree, confirming ignore-paths match failure is caused by un-normalized paths (e.g. leading './') reaching the ignore-list regex check before os.path.normpath is applied

aspects.where: pylint-dev/pylint GitHub repository issues, PRs, and commit history around version 2.14-2.15

aspects.name: recursive-flag-implementation
aspects.question: How does the --recursive flag process directories, and where in the code path does it diverge from non-recursive behavior?
aspects.where: pylint codebase - argument parsing, file discovery, and the recursive directory traversal logic

aspects.name: code_path_recursive
aspects.question: Where in the codebase does recursive mode discover and expand modules? Does it use a different code path than non-recursive mode?
aspects.where: pylint/lint/ directory, specifically looking for expand_modules, _iterate_file_descrs, or similar discovery functions. Check how --recursive flag is processed and what it does differently.

aspects.name: ignore_paths_application
aspects.question: Where and when are ignore-paths patterns applied? Is there a point in the recursive discovery where ignore-paths should be checked but isn't?
aspects.where: Where expand_modules is called, where file paths are filtered. Look for uses of ignore-paths config and regex matching against discovered paths.

aspects.name: config_loading
aspects.question: Is ignore-paths correctly loaded from pyproject.toml in all execution modes? Could the config be loaded but not passed to the recursive discovery function?
aspects.where: pylint/config/ and pylint/lint/base_options.py where ignore-paths is defined. Trace how config flows from loading to the expand_modules call.

aspects.name: upstream_issues
aspects.question: Has this bug been reported, discussed, or fixed in the project's issue tracker? Are there related PRs or commits?
aspects.where: GitHub issues for pylint-dev/pylint, searching for 'recursive ignore-paths', 'recursive ignore', '--recursive ignore', around version 2.14.1 and 2.15 timeframe.

aspects.name: ignore-paths-mechanism
aspects.question: How does the ignore-paths configuration get compiled into regex patterns and applied?
aspects.where: Configuration loading in pylint/config, the ignore_paths option definition, and the _is_ignored_file function in expand_modules.py

corpus.rationale: Small corpus justified: this is a focused configuration bug with clear dimensions. We need to test combinations of pattern types, recursive modes, and config locations. 10 instances cover the critical paths without redundancy.

fom.measure: Run hidden target tests that verify ignore-paths is respected when --recursive=y is used. The metric is the fraction of target tests passing (0.0 to 1.0). Since we cannot see the tests, we validate with: (1) manual reproduction showing src/gen/* is ignored with --recursive=y and ignore-paths pattern; (2) existing pylint test suite passes with no regressions.
fom.name: target_tests_passing

instances.behaviour: With --ignore=ignore style basename ignoring configured via pylintrc, running pylint in recursive mode over a project whose ignored module sits at a top-level-file location invoked with a relative target path must not emit lint messages for the ignored module, and must still lint the non-ignored module normally.
instances.command:
set -e
WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$WORK/src/gen"
printf 'x = 1\n' > "$WORK/src/gen/about.py"
printf 'y = 2\n' > "$WORK/src/main.py"
if [ "top-level-file" = "nested-package-init" ]; then
  touch "$WORK/src/gen/__init__.py"
fi
if [ "pylintrc" = "pylintrc" ]; then
  printf '[MASTER]\nignore=about.py\n' > "$WORK/.pylintrc"
else
  printf '[tool.pylint.MASTER]\nignore = ["about.py"]\n' > "$WORK/pyproject.toml"
fi
if [ "relative" = "absolute" ]; then
  TARGET="$WORK/src"
else
  TARGET="src"
fi
cd "$WORK"
if [ "recursive" = "recursive" ]; then
  python -m pylint --recursive=y "$TARGET" > out.txt 2>&1 || true
else
  python -m pylint "$TARGET" "$TARGET/gen" > out.txt 2>&1 || true
fi
grep -q "main.py" out.txt && ! grep -q "about.py" out.txt
instances.name: pylintrc-ignore-relative-recursive-top-level-file

instances.behaviour: With target_type=single_file, ignore-paths pattern variant 'matches_target' set via cli, and --recursive=y, pylint invoked directly on a single .py file must apply ignore-paths correctly: the file's unused-import message is suppressed iff the pattern matches the file path, regardless of the recursive flag (single-file targets bypass directory recursion entirely, so this must hold both before and after any recursive-walk fix).
instances.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re, sys, tempfile, subprocess
work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="plx7080_")
target = os.path.join(work, "gen_module.py")
with open(target, "w") as f:
    f.write("import os\n")
patterns = {
    "matches_target": r"^.*gen_module\.py$",
    "no_match": r"^.*other_module\.py$",
    "matches_everything": r".*",
    "matches_nothing": r"^$",
}
pattern = patterns["matches_target"]
should_ignore = bool(re.match(pattern, target)) or bool(re.match(pattern, os.path.basename(target)))
args = [sys.executable, "-m", "pylint", "--disable=all", "--enable=unused-import",
        "--recursive=y"]
if "cli" == "cli":
    args += ["--ignore-paths", pattern]
else:
    rcpath = os.path.join(work, "pylintrc")
    with open(rcpath, "w") as f:
        f.write("[MASTER]\nignore-paths=%s\n" % pattern)
    args += ["--rcfile", rcpath]
args.append(target)
proc = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=work)
matched = "unused-import" in proc.stdout
ok = (not matched) if should_ignore else matched
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
PY

instances.behaviour: With target_type=single_file, ignore-paths pattern variant 'matches_nothing' set via cli, and --recursive=n, pylint invoked directly on a single .py file must apply ignore-paths correctly: the file's unused-import message is suppressed iff the pattern matches the file path, regardless of the recursive flag (single-file targets bypass directory recursion entirely, so this must hold both before and after any recursive-walk fix).
instances.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re, sys, tempfile, subprocess
work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="plx7080_")
target = os.path.join(work, "gen_module.py")
with open(target, "w") as f:
    f.write("import os\n")
patterns = {
    "matches_target": r"^.*gen_module\.py$",
    "no_match": r"^.*other_module\.py$",
    "matches_everything": r".*",
    "matches_nothing": r"^$",
}
pattern = patterns["matches_nothing"]
should_ignore = bool(re.match(pattern, target)) or bool(re.match(pattern, os.path.basename(target)))
args = [sys.executable, "-m", "pylint", "--disable=all", "--enable=unused-import",
        "--recursive=n"]
if "cli" == "cli":
    args += ["--ignore-paths", pattern]
else:
    rcpath = os.path.join(work, "pylintrc")
    with open(rcpath, "w") as f:
        f.write("[MASTER]\nignore-paths=%s\n" % pattern)
    args += ["--rcfile", rcpath]
args.append(target)
proc = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=work)
matched = "unused-import" in proc.stdout
ok = (not matched) if should_ignore else matched
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

instances.name: rcfile-matches-nothing-n-single-file

instances.behaviour: With ignore-paths matching a single file (pkg/gen_file.py) via a anchored regex set through pyproject_toml, pylint --recursive=y must not report any messages for gen_file.py, while still linting pkg/module.py normally.
instances.command:
set -e
D=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$D/pkg"
cat > "$D/pkg/gen_file.py" <<'EOF'
import os,sys
x=1
EOF
cat > "$D/pkg/module.py" <<'EOF'
"""doc"""


def foo():
    return 1
EOF
touch "$D/pkg/__init__.py"
cat > "$D/pyproject.toml" <<'EOF'
[tool.pylint.MASTER]
ignore-paths = ["^pkg/gen_file\.py$"]
EOF
cd "$D" && python -m pylint --recursive=y pkg 2>&1 | grep -q "gen_file.py" && exit 1 || exit 0
instances.expected: fail_before_fix

instances.command:
set -e
WORKDIR="tmp/research/pylint7080_c52_ignore-paths_yes_excluded"
rm -rf "$WORKDIR"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR/gen52"
if [ "yes" = "yes" ]; then touch "$WORKDIR/gen52/__init__.py"; fi
printf 'import os\n' > "$WORKDIR/gen52/bad.py"
printf 'import sys\n' > "$WORKDIR/good.py"
case "ignore-paths" in
  ignore-paths) OPT="--ignore-paths=^.*gen52.*$" ;;
  ignore) OPT="--ignore=gen52" ;;
  ignore-patterns) OPT="--ignore-patterns=gen52" ;;
esac
( cd "$WORKDIR" && python -m pylint --recursive=y --disable=all --enable=unused-import "$OPT" . > out.txt 2>&1 || true )
if [ "excluded" = "excluded" ]; then
  ! grep -q "gen52/bad.py" "$WORKDIR/out.txt"
else
  grep -q "good.py" "$WORKDIR/out.txt"
fi

set -e
WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d)
if [ "top_level_dir" = "nested_dir" ]; then GENDIR="$WORKDIR/src/m54_gen"; else GENDIR="$WORKDIR/m54_gen"; fi
mkdir -p "$GENDIR"
printf 'import os\n' > "$GENDIR/bad.py"
printf 'import sys\n' > "$WORKDIR/good.py"
if [ "anchored_regex" = "anchored_regex" ]; then PATTERN="^.*m54_gen/.*$"; else PATTERN="m54_gen"; fi
CFGARGS=""
case "pyproject_toml" in
  pyproject_toml)
    printf '[tool.pylint.MASTER]\nignore-paths = ["%s"]\n' "$PATTERN" > "$WORKDIR/pyproject.toml"
    ;;
  pylintrc)
    printf '[MASTER]\nignore-paths=%s\n' "$PATTERN" > "$WORKDIR/.pylintrc"
    ;;
  cli_flag)
    CFGARGS="--ignore-paths=$PATTERN"
    ;;
esac
cd "$WORKDIR"
OUT=$(python -m pylint --recursive=y $CFGARGS . 2>&1 || true)
if echo "$OUT" | grep -q "bad.py"; then echo "FAIL: bad.py flagged"; exit 1; fi
